target_customer: Hong Kong and Southeast Asian restaurants and F&B operators
problem: Restaurants face staff shortages, costly ingredients and no data analysis; they need ordering, payments, supplier ordering and financing in one system.
business_model: Restaurant POS SaaS plus payments, delivery app commission, supplier ordering and short-term loans

founders.name: Tim Lee
previous_startups: Ran a cafe and a Japanese restaurant
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; HKTDC article says he moved from finance to catering.

founders.name: Ben Wong
previous_startups: Ran a 20-staff Japanese restaurant and bubble tea shops
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; expertise in payment clearing, loan models and cash management.

competitors.name: Eats365
competitors.what: Hong Kong cloud POS and online ordering suite for F&B, started as an HKSTP incubatee

competitors.name: Aigens
competitors.what: QR code ordering and F&B digital platform across Hong Kong, Singapore and Malaysia, founded 2012
competitors.traction_then: over 500 F&B brands (as of its December 2022 announcement)

technical_complexity.rationale: POS, ordering and delivery apps are standard; payments and lending add compliance work but use partners such as Stripe and Global Payments.

defensibility.rationale: POS switching costs are real once installed, but local rivals existed and the product is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Aigens raised a $14M Series A led by Ant Group in December 2022, after the batch.

market_need_then: Hong Kong F&B faced labor shortages and COVID-driven shift to online ordering and delivery, per the HKTDC founder story.

identity.voice_and_tone: LinkedIn tagline: we let the chef be chef

branding.brand_signature: Tagline: we let the chef be chef (LinkedIn page)
branding.community_and_virality: Became the official Hong Kong agent for Meituan Dianping and appeared at HOFEX 2023 per search results; no fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Local B2B and consumer delivery brand with some trade press (HKTDC), but no sourced evidence of strong pull.

outcome_analysis: DimOrder was founded by two restaurant operators, giving it founder-market fit, and now runs a team of about 70 with POS, delivery and payment products across offices in Hong Kong, Thailand, Taipei and Guangzhou. No shutdown or acquisition was found. Funding is unverified, so growth quality cannot be judged.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators show $629K from YC and ParticleX, a $4.5M four-round total and a 2020 $1.3M seed (Seedtable); none confirmed. The company site lists investors Y Combinator, Gravity, ParticleX, Cyberport, AppWorks, K3, Founders HK and Pareto without amounts. A $7.4M 2024 revenue figure comes from a low-quality aggregator. Aigens source is dated after the batch (Dec 2022). The company site did not name founders; HKTDC says three founders. Completeness pass: a 1.3M seed dated 2020-11 is recorded from Seedtable alone, a single database; Bouncewatch also lists 1.9M (2021-09) and 1.3M (2022-03) for a 4.5M total, and another profile says 629K, so these are not recorded and amounts conflict.
